title: I Enforced the Judo-Mat Hygiene Log on the Sensei's Barefoot Nephew

parts.text: I bowed on at 5:09 p.m. and sensei Nori's nephew was already barefoot off the hygiene tray. The board said: FEET ON THE TRAY. LOG THE WIPE. NO BARE CUTS. I was thirty-two, adult beginner, holding a hygiene card. Nori shrugged. "Family is the dojo." I photographed the board, the card, and the bare prints. Then I asked for the mat log. At 5:15 the club chair pinged why Nori's name was on skipped wipes. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The club chair can see bare prints off the tray on the judo hygiene log.

social.video_title: The sensei's nephew skipped the mat hygiene tray — Part 1/2
social.description: Judo dojo, a wipe board, bare prints. I logged the skip. Would you have asked the chair?

parts.text: Nori called it tradition until the chair asked for the still. I printed the log, the board, and the photo. The nephew used the tray. Nori ran family through hygiene and told the next sensei tradition was always about optics. Optics is a word senseis use when trays exist. Log policy now has a second line: NEPHEWS USE THE TRAY. I keep the card. Nori brown-bags the jokes. The tatami finally looks like a board, not a living room. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Mat log, wiped feet, and a second line. Was tradition ever the tray?
